title: High-resolution mapping of mitotic DNA synthesis under conditions of replication stress in cultured cells
protocol: Seed 1.25 × 10^6 H1299 cells per T175 flask (15 flasks per condition).
Place cells in the incubator for 48 h.
Treat cells with 1.5 mM thymidine.
Place cells in the incubator for 16 h.
Wash cells three times with 10 ml PBS.
Add 12 ml pre-warmed culture medium supplemented with 6 μM RO-3306 and 0.2 μM aphidicolin per flask.
Place cells in the incubator for 10.5 h.
Treat cells with 2 mM hydroxyurea.
Incubate cells for 1.5 hours.
Wash cells three times with pre-warmed culture medium supplemented with 2 mM hydroxyurea.
Add 12 mL of pre-warmed culture medium per flask, supplemented with 2 mM hydroxyurea, 100 ng/mL nocodazole, and 10 μM EdU.
Incubate cells for 1.5 hours.
Perform a mitotic shake-off to detach loosely attached mitotic cells without detaching interphase cells.
Collect the medium containing floating mitotic cells in 50-mL tubes.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Wash cells with PBS.
Transfer cell pellets to one 15-mL tube per condition.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend cell pellets in 1 mL PBS.
Pipette up and down several times to obtain a single-cell solution.
Vortex the cell solution at low speed.
Add ice-cold methanol dropwise to achieve a final concentration of 90% (v/v).
Place fixed cells on ice for at least 1 h.
Centrifuge cells at 350 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Wash cell pellets with 3 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge cells at 350 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellets in 1 mL permeabilization buffer per 3 × 10^6 cells.
Incubate the cell suspension at room temperature for 30 min.
Centrifuge cells at 350 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Wash cells with 3 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge cells at 350 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Prepare the biotin-azide ‘click’ reaction cocktail according to specifications.
Resuspend cell pellets in 250 μL of biotin-azide click reaction cocktail per 3 × 10^6 cells.
Incubate cell suspensions for 30 min at room temperature and in the dark.
Centrifuge cells at 350 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Wash cells with 3 mL PBS.
Resuspend cells in 400 μL lysis buffer.
Transfer cells to a 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate samples in a water bath at 50°C for at least 3 h.
Add 1 volume (400 μL) of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1).
Mix by flicking and transfer to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Spin in a microcentrifuge at maximum speed for 5 min, at room temperature.
Recover the aqueous phase and transfer to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Add 1 volume (400 μL) of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol.
Mix by inverting.
Spin in a microcentrifuge at maximum speed for 5 min at room temperature.
Recover the aqueous phase without touching the interphase and transfer to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Add NaCl to achieve a final concentration of 0.2 M (add 16 μL of 5 M NaCl).
Mix well.
Add 1 μL of glycogen as carrier.
Precipitate the DNA by adding 832 μL of ice-cold ethanol.
Incubate for 2 hours at -20°C.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatants, being careful not to disrupt the pellets.
Wash with 70% ice-cold ethanol.
Spin in a micro-centrifuge at maximum speed for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatants, being careful not to disrupt the pellets.
Let the pellet dry for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add 55 μL TE buffer.
Allow the DNA to resuspend at room temperature for several hours.
Measure the DNA concentration using a Qubit fluorometer with dsDNA BR assay kit.
Transfer 5–15 μg of DNA to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Adjust the volume to 105 μL with water.
Retrieve 5 ng DNA as chromatin input sample for baseline sequencing profiles (optional).
Use a bioruptor to sonicate the DNA into fragments of 100–500 bp.
Optimize the bioruptor settings to obtain DNA fragments of 250 bp in length.
Run 2 μL of sonicated DNA on a 1% agarose gel.
Assess the length of DNA fragment using gel imaging system.
Resuspend Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 beads by vortexing.
Transfer 50 μL of bead suspension to one 1.5-mL tube per sample.
Place the tube on the magnet for 1–2 min.
Carefully aspirate and discard the preservative solution while the tube is on the magnet.
Wash the beads with 50 μL of 1× BW buffer.
Resuspend the beads by vortexing at low speed.
Perform a short spin (1,000 × g, 20°C, 5 s).
Place the tube on the magnet for 1–2 min.
Carefully aspirate and discard the supernatants while the tube is on the magnet.
Repeat washing steps two more times.
Resuspend the beads in 100 μL of 2× BW buffer.
Transfer 100 μL of beads to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Add 100 μL of sonicated DNA.
Incubate samples for 15 min at room temperature on a rotating wheel.
Place the tube on the magnet for 1–2 minutes.
Aspirate and discard the supernatants while the tube is on the magnet.
Remove the tube from the magnet and wash the beads with 200 μL of 1×BW buffer.
Resuspend the beads by vortexing at low speed.
Perform a short spin (1,000 × g, 20°C, 5 seconds).
Place the tube on the magnet for 1–2 minutes.
Aspirate and discard the supernatants while the tube is on the magnet.
Repeat the washing steps two more times.
Remove the tube from the magnet and wash the beads with 200 μL of TE.
Resuspend the beads by vortexing at low speed.
Perform a short spin (1,000 × g, 20°C, 5 seconds).
Place the tube on the magnet for 1–2 minutes.
Aspirate and discard the supernatants while the tube is on the magnet.
Remove the tube from the magnet and add 55 μL of elution solution (2-β-mercaptoethanol).
Resuspend the beads by pipetting.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Place the samples on the magnet for 1–2 minutes.
Recover the supernatants, which contain the eluted EdU-labeled DNA, while the tube is on the magnet.
Transfer to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Measure the DNA concentration with a Qubit fluorometer using dsDNA BR assay kit and 5 μL of each sample.
Use 5 ng of eluted DNA to prepare sequencing libraries according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Perform high-throughput 100-bp single-end sequencing using an Illumina Hi-Seq 4000 sequencer, aiming for at least 20 × 10^6 reads per sample.
Optional: Perform the library preparation and high-throughput sequencing steps for the chromatin input samples as well.
